paper.title: Nonstochastic Bandits with Composite Anonymous Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Nonstochastic K-armed bandits with d-delayed composite anonymous feedback
unmapped: Composite anonymous feedback: the loss of the action played at time t is adversarially split into d+1 nonnegative components charged at times t,...,t+d; the learner observes only the sum of components arriving at each round, not the individual components or which action they belong to
D (paper's d) is a known upper bound on the maximum delay/spread
Regret is defined on composite losses against playing a fixed action in all rounds
settings.definition_quote: the loss $\loss_t(i) \in [0,1]$ at time $t$ of an action $i \in [K]$ is defined by the sum $\loss_t(i) \coloneqq \sum_{s=0}^{d} \loss_t^{(s)}(i)$ of $(d+1)$-many components ... what the player observes at the end of each round $t$ is only the composite loss $\lcomp_t(I_{t-d},\dots,I_t)$.

algorithms.name: CoLoWrapper (Composite Loss Wrapper) with generic xi-stable base algorithm

symbols.beta_b: bias of the i.i.d. Bernoulli sequence B driving block endpoints
symbols.xi: stability parameter of the base algorithm (expected positive-part change of its distribution per update)
symbols.R_base: worst-case regret of the base algorithm after floor(T/(2D+1)) rounds on [0,1]-valued adversarial losses

tuning: B i.i.d. Bernoulli(beta) independent of base algorithm randomization, beta in (0,1)

source.label: t:regret-CoLoWr
source.quote: If we run \colowr{} with a $\xi$-stable base $K$-armed bandit algorithm $\alpha$ and an i.i.d.\ sequence $\bb = (B_t)_{t\in \N}$ of Bernoulli random variables with bias $\beta\in (0,1)$ (independent of the randomization of $\alpha$), then, for any time horizon $T \ge 2d + 1$, the regret $R_T$ satisfies R_T <= 2d + \frac{2d+1}{d+1} ( 3d + 2d\beta(1-\beta)^{2d} \xi T + \frac{1}{\beta(1-\beta)^{2d}} \cR_{\lfl{ T/(2d+1) }} )

results.notes: Reduction bound; paper's d mapped to D (delay). Horizon marked anytime since wrapper does not use T, but base regret term may depend on tuning. Text also states (informally) an O(sqrt((d+1)KT log K)) bound with Exp3 base (eta-stable, Lemma 14).

source.label: c:main-result
source.quote: For any time horizon $T\in \N$, if we run \colowr{} using: As $\alpha$, \Cref{a:jake} with learning rate $\eta = \sqrt{\frac 1 2 \lfl{\fracc T {(2d+1)}}}$; As $\bb$, an i.i.d.\ sequence of Bernoulli random variables with bias $\beta = \frac 1 {2d+1}$ ... then, its regret satisfies R_T \le c \sqrt{(d+1)KT} where $c = 2\sqrt{2}$ if $d=0$, and $c = 28$ otherwise.

results.notes: Paper's d is the delay, mapped to D.

source.label: c:main-result
source.quote: ... then, its regret satisfies R_T \le c \sqrt{(d+1)KT} where $c = 2\sqrt{2}$ if $d=0$, and $c = 28$ otherwise.

results.notes: d=0 case reduces to standard bandit with FTRL-Tsallis (Abernethy et al. bound).

conditions: Omega_tilde hides a sqrt(log T) denominator
T multiple of d+1 (otherwise additive O(d+1))

source.label: t:lower
source.quote: For any algorithm $A_d$ for $K$-armed bandits with $d$-delayed composite anonymous feedback, $\cR_T(A_d,K,d)=\widetilde{\Omega}\big(\sqrt{(d+1)KT}\big)$.

results.notes: Via reduction from linear bandits on the simplex (Lemma 8) and Shamir (2015) lower bound (Lemma 9). Worst-case over oblivious loss components.
